lead: They have accused the mayor of corruption.
explanation: Active 'they have accused him of' becomes passive: has been accused of.

lead: 'I broke the window,' the boy said.
sentence: When caught, the boy ___ the window.
explanation: admit + -ing, or admit having + past participle for the earlier action.

lead: It wasn't necessary for her to bring any food — there was plenty.
explanation: needn't have + participle = it wasn't necessary, but she did it.

lead: She started working here five years ago.
explanation: Action continuing from a past point to now: has been working (present perfect continuous).

lead: I haven't seen a better film this year.
sentence: This is ___ I've seen this year.
explanation: I haven't seen a better film = this is the best film (that) I've seen.

lead: 'Don't touch the paintings in this room,' the guide warned us.
sentence: The guide warned ___ the paintings in that room.
explanation: Negative commands are reported with warned + object + not to + infinitive.

lead: He couldn't swim until he was twenty.
sentence: He ___ swim until he was twenty.
explanation: couldn't = was not able to (general ability in the past).

lead: The suitcase was so heavy that I couldn't lift it.
sentence: It was ___ that I couldn't lift it.
explanation: so + adjective + that → such (+a) + adjective + noun + that.

lead: I'd love to be lying on a beach right now.
sentence: I ___ lying on a beach right now.
explanation: wish + past subjunctive: I wish I were (formal 'were', not 'was').

lead: People say the castle is haunted.
explanation: People say X is… → X is said to be…

lead: Although he is remarkably rich, he lives very simply.
explanation: Although he may be rich → Rich as (he) may be — fronted adjective + as + may.

lead: She prefers reading books to watching television.
explanation: prefer X to Y = would rather do X than do Y.

lead: Selling the boat was a big mistake.
explanation: should(n't) have + participle expresses regret about a past action.

lead: They won't let you in without a ticket.
explanation: let somebody do → be allowed to do: won't be allowed in.

lead: He didn't study, so he failed the exam.
sentence: If he had studied, he ___ the exam.
explanation: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

lead: 'I'll definitely call you when I land,' she told me.
explanation: Reported promise: promised to call; the person promised shifts to 'me'.

lead: A mechanic repaired my father's roof last week.
explanation: have something done = arrange for somebody to do it: had his roof repaired.

lead: After a year in Paris, the pace of life feels normal to her.
sentence: She ___ the pace of life in Paris.
explanation: get used to + noun/-ing = become accustomed to; present perfect for present result.

lead: What is the fee for annual membership?
sentence: How much ___ pay for annual membership?
explanation: have to for external obligation: How much do you have to pay?

lead: The party was incredibly boring, so we left early.
sentence: The party was ___ we left early.
explanation: so + adjective + that-clause expresses result.

lead: I last visited Rome in 2019.
explanation: last did X in (year) = haven't done X since (year).

lead: Nobody else in the team runs as fast as Maya.
explanation: nobody runs faster = she is the fastest runner.

lead: 'Did you send the invoice?' the manager asked her.
explanation: if/whether + subject + backshifted verb: whether she had sent.

lead: You can borrow the car, but you must drive it carefully.
sentence: You can borrow the car ___ it carefully.
explanation: provided (that) introduces the condition.

lead: The journey was so tiring that we slept all day.
sentence: It was ___ that we slept all day.
explanation: so tiring (a journey) → such a tiring journey.

lead: I rarely drink coffee in the evening.
explanation: be (not) used to something = (not) accustomed to it.

lead: The garage is servicing my car tomorrow morning.
explanation: Arranged service: have/get something done — having my car serviced.

lead: He spoke so quietly that the jury couldn't hear him.
sentence: He spoke ___ for the jury to hear him.
explanation: so quietly that nobody could hear = too quietly (for anybody) to hear.

lead: I regret not bringing an umbrella.
explanation: Regret about the past: wish + subject + had + participle.

lead: 'We are closing the factory,' the board announced.
sentence: The board announced that ___ the factory.
explanation: we → they; present continuous → past continuous: they were closing.

lead: He can't be in Spain — I saw him here this morning.
sentence: He ___ in Spain — I saw him this morning.
explanation: can't/cannot possibly be = it is impossible that he is.

lead: The guidebook says this bridge is Roman.
explanation: be supposed to be = generally said or believed to be.

lead: I only understood the pattern much later.
explanation: Front 'only + time phrase' forces inversion: Only much later did I understand.

lead: Someone must check this equipment before every flight.
explanation: must check → must be checked (modal + be + past participle).

lead: 'I'm sorry I kept you waiting,' she said.
explanation: apologise for doing something: apologised for keeping me waiting.

lead: Fewer students enrolled this year than we expected.
explanation: fewer than expected = not as many (students) as expected.

lead: We couldn't see the lighthouse anywhere.
explanation: Fronted 'nowhere' forces inversion: Nowhere could we see…

lead: She'll be on a flight, so she can't join the call.
sentence: She'll be on a flight, so ___ join the call.
explanation: won't be able to = future inability.

lead: 'You copied my design!' she told him.
explanation: accuse somebody OF doing something.

lead: There isn't a single clean cup left in the cupboard.
hint: run out of = have none left
explanation: run out of = have no more of something left.

lead: You didn't tell me about the meeting, and you should have.
sentence: You really ___ me about the meeting.
explanation: ought to have + participle = should have done (but didn't).

lead: The plane takes one hour; the train takes two.
explanation: half the time = twice as fast as.

lead: He would rather not talk about the accident.
explanation: would prefer + not + to-infinitive.

lead: 'I have never lied to the press,' the minister said.
explanation: deny + -ing (ever strengthens the denial): denied ever lying.

lead: 'I will definitely complete the report by Friday,' I said.
explanation: commit oneself TO + -ing: committed myself to finishing.

lead: People believe she was the finest pianist of her generation.
sentence: She ___ the finest pianist of her generation.
explanation: A present belief about a past event: is thought to have + participle.

lead: Perhaps she never received our message.
explanation: may/might have + participle = possibility in the past.

lead: He had just sat down when the phone rang.
explanation: No sooner had + subject + participle … than…

lead: I'd like to move to a place where nobody knows me.
sentence: I'd like to move ___ nobody knows me.
explanation: 'somewhere (…) where' = a place in which.

lead: The bad weather meant we couldn't leave the house.
explanation: prevent somebody FROM doing something.

lead: 'Why don't we hold the wedding outdoors?' said Ana.
explanation: suggest + that-clause, or suggest + -ing: suggested they hold / suggested holding.

lead: The police believe the two suspects left the country.
explanation: A present belief about a past event: are believed to have + participle.

lead: I have never heard such a ridiculous excuse.
explanation: Fronted 'never' forces inversion: Never have I heard…

lead: The doctor said that he should take a complete rest.
sentence: The doctor advised ___ a complete rest.
explanation: say + should → advise + object + to-infinitive: advised him to take.

lead: The ceremony will take place in the cathedral.
explanation: Ceremonies are held: will be held (in a venue).

lead: Jogging every morning was completely normal for him.
explanation: be used to + -ing = be accustomed to.

lead: The flat was too cramped for their three children.
sentence: The flat wasn't ___ their three children.
explanation: too cramped for = not spacious enough for.

lead: 'You mustn't run near the pool,' the lifeguard told the children.
sentence: The lifeguard told the children ___ near the pool.
explanation: told + object + not to + infinitive.

lead: The instructions only made sense after she had read them twice.
sentence: The instructions ___ sense until she had read them twice.
explanation: made sense only after = didn't make sense until.

lead: It was unfair of the referee to send him off.
explanation: should(n't) have + participle criticises a past decision.

lead: I'd love to be able to afford a bigger flat.
explanation: wish + subject + could expresses regret about ability or possibility.

lead: My advice is to check the contract twice before signing.
sentence: You ___ the contract twice before signing.
explanation: had better + infinitive without 'to' = strong advice.

lead: 'Could you open the window, please?' she asked me.
explanation: Reported request: asked + object + to-infinitive.

lead: The concert was cancelled because hardly anybody came.
sentence: The concert was cancelled ___ people came.
explanation: because so few people came = because hardly anybody came.

lead: He finally succeeded in solving the puzzle.
explanation: manage to do = be able to do.

lead: The soup needed a little more salt.
explanation: needed a little more = didn't have enough (salt).

lead: 'I never wrote that review,' the chef insisted.
explanation: deny + -ing: denied ever writing (strong denial).

lead: We packed a spare tyre because the road might be bad.
sentence: We packed a spare tyre ___ bad.
hint: in case = because it might happen
explanation: in case + clause = as a precaution against a possibility.

lead: Travelling off-peak costs considerably less.
explanation: costs less = is less expensive; 'considerably' keeps the degree.

lead: He began playing chess at the age of six.
sentence: He ___ at the age of six.
explanation: take up = start (a hobby or sport): took up chess.

lead: I wish I had never told her the secret.
explanation: wish + past perfect ≈ shouldn't have + participle.

lead: 'Shall I carry that for you?' he asked.
explanation: offer to do something: offered to carry it.

lead: The plane left the runway moments before the storm hit.
sentence: The plane had ___ the storm hit.
explanation: had just + participle = a moment before.

lead: Her French improved because she spent years in Lyon.
sentence: Her French improved as ___ in Lyon.
explanation: as a result of + noun/-ing = because of.

lead: Parking here is strictly forbidden.
explanation: strictly forbidden = must never (+ infinitive).

lead: It took the artist three weeks to paint the mural.
explanation: it took X time to do = X spent time doing: spent over three weeks on.

lead: 'I've never been to Asia,' she told me.
sentence: She told me that ___ to Asia.
explanation: Present perfect shifts to past perfect in reported speech.

lead: He enjoys his work despite his low salary.
explanation: 'though' can close a sentence as a soft 'however'.

lead: I can't wait for the holidays to start.
explanation: look forward TO + -ing: the 'to' is a preposition.

lead: Nobody can say that he doesn't work hard.
explanation: deny that + clause (or deny + -ing, formal).

lead: You must complete the form in ink.
explanation: must complete → must be completed (modal + be + participle).

lead: That's the school where my mother teaches.
explanation: where = in which in formal relative clauses.

lead: She left early because she didn't want to miss the train.
explanation: so as not to / in order not to + infinitive.

lead: The tickets are certain to be expensive this year.
explanation: be bound to do = be certain to do.

lead: A long, dry summer caused the famine.
sentence: The famine ___ a long, dry summer.
explanation: A causes B = B results from A (note the direction).

lead: 'Would you like to join us for dinner?' they asked him.
answer: invited him to join them for
explanation: invite somebody TO do something; pronouns shift in reporting.

lead: I haven't enjoyed myself so much for years.
sentence: It's ___ I've enjoyed myself so much.
explanation: It's (been) years since + past simple = I haven't done it for years.

lead: The athlete insisted that she had never taken banned substances.
explanation: deny having + past participle denies an earlier action.

lead: Somebody needs to renew this passport before June.
explanation: need + -ing = need to be + participle: needs renewing.

lead: Despite his serious injury, he finished the marathon.
explanation: in spite of + noun/-ing = despite.

lead: People claim that this herbal tea cures colds.
explanation: X is claimed to + infinitive = people claim X does.

lead: He is so impatient that he refuses to read instructions.
explanation: so impatient that he refuses = far too impatient to.

lead: They say the new tunnel will halve journey times.
sentence: Journey times ___ by the new tunnel.
explanation: X is said to be + participle: reported statement, passive meaning.

lead: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone about this.
explanation: keep something to yourself = tell nobody.

lead: The committee probably won't change the rules.
sentence: ___ the committee will change the rules.
explanation: probably won't = it is (highly) unlikely that.

lead: 'Have you seen my keys anywhere?' he asked us.
sentence: He asked us ___ his keys anywhere.
explanation: if/whether + subject + backshifted verb: whether we had seen.

lead: Visitors may not feed the animals.
explanation: may not = are (strictly) forbidden to.

lead: He was sacked for constantly missing deadlines.
sentence: If he hadn't kept missing deadlines, he ___ sacked.
explanation: If + past perfect, would(n't) have been + participle.

lead: 'I'm sorry I was so rude to your sister,' Maria said.
sentence: Maria apologised ___ so rude to my sister.
explanation: apologise for + -ing: apologised for being so rude.

lead: You can only get a seat if you book well in advance.
explanation: if you don't book = without booking.

lead: As well as speaking fluent French, she also speaks Russian.
explanation: in addition to = as well as.

lead: The hotel was further from the beach than we expected.
answer: as close to the beach as
explanation: further than expected = not as close (to the beach) as expected.

lead: The exam regulations forbid the use of mobile phones.
explanation: forbid = must never + be + participle (passive).

lead: My grandfather planted all these apple trees himself.
sentence: My grandfather is the ___ all these apple trees.
explanation: 'the one who…' identifies the agent with a relative clause.

lead: The results were announced, and immediately people began celebrating.
sentence: The results had ___ people began celebrating.
explanation: No sooner had the results been announced than people began…

lead: The tickets cost so much that we stayed at home.
sentence: They were ___ we stayed at home.
explanation: so much (money) → such expensive tickets (no article with plurals).

lead: The doctor persuaded me to promise that I would exercise daily.
sentence: The doctor ___ that I would exercise daily.
explanation: get somebody TO do something = persuade/make them.

lead: She cooked a huge meal, but we had already eaten.
explanation: needn't have + participle = it happened although it wasn't necessary.

lead: His trainers were so worn out that they had holes in them.
sentence: His trainers were ___ they had holes in them.
explanation: so worn out = in such bad condition.

lead: I'd prefer it if you arrived before eight.
explanation: would rather + subject + past simple for other people's actions.

lead: The rescue team managed to reach the village by helicopter.
sentence: The rescue team ___ the village by helicopter.
explanation: manage to do = succeed IN doing.

lead: Assembling the wardrobe took me two hours.
explanation: it took me X to do = I spent X doing.

lead: Although she was exhausted, she carried on working.
explanation: despite/in spite of + -ing: despite being exhausted.

lead: He had just got home when the power cut happened.
sentence: ___ home when the power cut happened.
explanation: Hardly had + subject + participle … when…

lead: You'll fail your exam if you don't revise.
explanation: unless + present simple = if you don't.

lead: Someone stole her bike last week.
explanation: have something stolen/done = experience it happening to you.

lead: You should start revising now.
explanation: it's (high) time + subject + past simple = you should already be doing it.

lead: He spoke slowly because he wanted us to understand him.
explanation: so that + subject + would/could expresses purpose.

lead: She hates it when people interrupt her.
explanation: hate + being + past participle (passive gerund).

lead: As I get older, I become less patient.
sentence: The older I get, ___ I become.
explanation: The older…, the more… — doubled comparatives for parallel change.

lead: Brian was really interested in North American history in his school days.
sentence: Brian ___ North American history in his school days.
hint: be interested in = have an ___ in
explanation: 'To be interested in' becomes the noun pattern: 'had an interest in'.

lead: Darius soon recovered after the operation on his knee and was able to rejoin the team.
sentence: After the operation on his knee, Darius ___ and was able to rejoin the team.
explanation: 'Recovered soon' is expressed with the noun: 'made a quick/fast/rapid recovery'.

lead: I always hated pasta when I was a child, but now I cook it regularly.
sentence: I ___ pasta when I was a child but now I cook it regularly.
explanation: 'used to + infinitive' describes a past state or habit that is no longer true.

lead: It was a mistake not to write the telephone number down.
sentence: I should ___ writing down the telephone number.
hint: make a point of doing = be sure to do
explanation: Regret about an omitted action: 'should have made a point of writing it down'.

lead: If Marc hadn't taken up politics, he might have become a famous art historian.
sentence: If Marc hadn't taken up politics, he might have ___ himself as an art historian.
hint: become famous = make a ___ for oneself
explanation: 'Make a name for himself' means become well known.

lead: This holiday is within our price range, provided we don't go to the expensive restaurants in the tourist centre.
sentence: We ___ as we avoid the expensive restaurants in the tourist centre.
answer: can afford this holiday as long
hint: provided = as long as; within our price range = can afford
explanation: 'Provided' is rewritten as 'as long as'; 'within our price range' as 'can afford'.

lead: Yesterday, I informed my boss in writing that I would be leaving the company.
hint: inform your employer in writing = hand in your ___
explanation: 'Hand in one's notice' means formally resign.

lead: It's very unlikely that Martin will win the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
sentence: Martin has almost ___ the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
explanation: 'It's very unlikely he will win' becomes 'he has almost no chance of winning'.

lead: Most of the children ignored what the teacher had told them.
sentence: Few of the children ___ what the teacher had told them.
explanation: 'Most ignored' becomes 'few took notice of'.

lead: The company is unable to guarantee an allocated car-parking space to all employees.
sentence: The company's employees shouldn't ___ allocated a car-parking space.
explanation: 'Count on being allocated' means rely on receiving.

lead: He no longer thinks he can find a job before the end of the year.
sentence: He has given ___ a job before the end of the year.
explanation: 'No longer thinks he can find' becomes 'has given up hope of finding'.

lead: I'm sure Jemma is going to become a famous model one day.
sentence: I think it's only ___ Jemma becomes a famous model.
explanation: 'It's only a matter of time before' means it will definitely happen eventually.

lead: I think learning to use a typewriter is a waste of time.
sentence: I can't ___ how to use a typewriter.
explanation: 'A waste of time' becomes 'can't see the point in/of doing it'.

lead: The company has a good reputation in the local area.
sentence: The company ___ of in the local area.
explanation: 'People speak highly of it' becomes the passive 'it is highly spoken of'.

lead: Nadia's friend arrived just as she was about to leave the restaurant.
sentence: Nadia was ___ the restaurant when her friend arrived.
hint: be about to = be on the point of + -ing
explanation: 'About to leave' becomes 'on the point of leaving'.

lead: I don't expect the company to make a profit this year, given the economic climate.
sentence: Given the economic climate, ___ the company made a profit this year.
hint: don't expect = would be surprised if + past
explanation: A tentative prediction: 'I would be surprised if + past simple'.

lead: Barbara's parents were certain that she would be a great tennis player.
sentence: Barbara's parents were ___ that she would be a great tennis player.
explanation: 'Certain' becomes 'in no doubt'.

lead: My grandfather had completely forgotten that he phoned me last night.
sentence: My grandfather didn't ___ phoning me last night.
explanation: 'Completely forgotten' becomes 'didn't have any recollection of'.

lead: Pay claims must be submitted before the end of the month.
sentence: You have ___ your pay claims before the end of the month.
explanation: 'Must be submitted' becomes 'you have to put in your claims'.

lead: At no time did we think that Pedro might be planning to leave the country.
sentence: It ___ that Pedro might be planning to leave the country.
hint: it occurred to sb = sb thought
explanation: 'At no time did we think' becomes 'it never occurred to us'.

lead: I'm sure we went the wrong way at the last junction.
hint: must have + participle for past deduction
explanation: A deduction about the past: 'must have taken'.

lead: We wanted to continue our mountain trek but the weather was too bad.
sentence: We ___ on with our mountain trek but the weather was too bad.
hint: unfulfilled wish: would have liked to
explanation: An unrealised wish about the past: 'would have liked to carry on'.

lead: No changes will be made to this project.
hint: go ahead = proceed; according to plan
explanation: 'No changes' means the project 'will go ahead according to plan'.

lead: Simon really ought to make a decision about his future.
sentence: It's high time Simon ___ about his future.
hint: it's high time + past; make a decision = make up one's mind
explanation: 'It's high time' takes the past subjunctive: 'made up his mind'.

lead: Phoebe was surprised to be offered a place on the course.
sentence: The offer of a place on the course ___ Phoebe.
hint: surprised by = come as a surprise to
explanation: 'Was surprised' becomes 'came as a surprise to her'.

lead: I can't deny that I was embarrassed to be given the award.
sentence: There's ___ embarrassment at being given the award.
explanation: 'There's no denying my embarrassment' = I can't deny I was embarrassed.

lead: Delia said that she would no longer tolerate her colleagues being rude.
sentence: 'I am not willing ___ from my colleagues any longer,' said Delia.
answer: to put up with any rudeness
explanation: 'Not willing to put up with rudeness' means will no longer tolerate it.

lead: It's difficult to know what my reaction would have been in that situation.
answer: sure how I would have reacted
hint: difficult to know = not sure how
explanation: 'I'm not sure how I would have reacted' — a hypothetical past.

lead: Do you mind if I come over to see you later?
sentence: Do you ___ coming over to see you later?
explanation: 'Have any objection to me/my coming' is the formal equivalent of 'do you mind'.

lead: Given that he has no experience, will Glyn be able to do this job?
sentence: Will Glyn's ___ his ability to do this job?
hint: no experience = lack of experience (noun subject)
explanation: The noun subject 'lack of experience' takes the verb 'affect'.
